title: What is Solace PubSub+: a message broker that supports hierarchical topic routing with level-aware wildcards (`*` matches one level, `>` matches one or more remaining levels): and how does it differ from Kafka's flat topic model (Solace routes at the broker using topic hierarchy; Kafka uses flat topics + consumer-side filtering or stream processing for fine-grained routing)?
shortTitle: What is Solace PubSub+, and how does its topic routing differ from Kafka's flat topics?
keyPoints: Solace PubSub+ is an enterprise message broker with hierarchical topic routing and level-aware wildcard subscriptions.
Solace topics are slash-separated strings attached at publish time, not pre-created broker objects.
The single-level wildcard (*) matches exactly one topic level; the multi-level wildcard (>) matches one or more remaining levels.
The Solace broker evaluates subscriptions and delivers only matching messages, so routing intelligence lives in the broker.
Kafka uses flat, pre-created topics where the broker does no content-based routing and consumers filter on their own.
Solace shifts routing CPU to the broker; Kafka shifts it to the consumer in exchange for massive throughput and replay.
A common enterprise pattern uses Solace for live selective routing and Kafka as the durable replayable backbone.

s1_definition.oneliner: Solace routes messages at the broker using a hierarchical topic structure and level-aware wildcards, while Kafka uses flat topics and pushes fine-grained filtering to the consumer.
s1_definition.profdef:
Solace PubSub+ and Kafka handle topic routing in fundamentally different ways.

- **Solace PubSub+** – an enterprise message broker that routes messages using hierarchical, slash-separated topic strings with level-aware wildcard subscriptions evaluated by the broker itself.
- **Hierarchical topic** – a publish-time string like `txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large` where each slash-separated level carries a routing dimension.
- **Single-level wildcard (*)** – matches exactly one level in a Solace topic subscription.
- **Multi-level wildcard (>)** – matches one or more remaining levels at the end of a Solace subscription.
- **Kafka flat topic** – a pre-created, named, partitioned log where the broker does no content-based routing and consumers read entire partitions.
s1_definition.analogy: At National Bank of India, Solace is like a mail system where every letter has a precise hierarchical address: transactions, Mumbai branch, savings accounts, large amounts. A desk can say "give me everything from Mumbai regardless of type" and the sorting office understands the structure and delivers only matching letters. Kafka is like having a few big labelled bins: everything goes into the transactions bin, and if you only want Mumbai large transactions you must pull out every letter and check it yourself, because the bin does not understand the address structure.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Solace Hierarchical Routing:

  Publisher ──► txn/IN/Mumbai/savings/large
                        │
               ┌────────▼────────┐
               │  Solace Broker   │
               │  (trie matcher)  │
               └────────┬────────┘
                        │
          ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
          │             │             │
     txn/IN/Mumbai/>  txn/IN/*/savings/large  txn/IN/Delhi/>
     (Priya: all      (Pankaj: all large     (no match,
      Mumbai txns)     savings across         not delivered)
                       India)

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Kafka Flat Topic:

  Publisher ──► bank.transactions [partition 0][partition 1][partition 2]
                        │
               ┌────────▼────────┐
               │  Kafka Broker    │
               │  (no filtering)  │
               └────────┬────────┘
                        │
          ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
          │             │             │
     Consumer A      Consumer B    Consumer C
     (reads ALL,     (reads ALL,   (reads ALL,
      filters in      filters in    filters in
      app code)       app code)     app code)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Solace PubSub+ is an enterprise message broker whose defining feature is hierarchical topic routing with level-aware wildcard subscriptions. Publishers attach structured, slash-separated topic strings to each message, and subscribers express interest using wildcards: `*` matches exactly one level and `>` matches one or more remaining levels. The broker itself evaluates every message against all active subscriptions and delivers only matching messages, so the routing intelligence lives in the broker and consumers stay thin.

Kafka takes the opposite approach and keeps the broker deliberately simple. A Kafka topic is a flat, pre-created, partitioned log, the broker never interprets structure inside the topic name or the message content, and a consumer subscribes to a whole topic and reads every record in its partitions. If you want only a narrow slice, you either filter in the consumer, create many fine-grained topics, or add a stream-processing layer.

At National Bank of India, the difference was practical. Desks that needed specific slices of the live transaction feed, like all Mumbai events or all large savings transactions, used Solace subscriptions and the broker delivered exactly the matching messages. The same feed flowed into a single flat Kafka topic for seven-year compliance retention and analytics, where each consumer filtered in application code.

Remember one sentence: Solace routes at the broker with hierarchical wildcards so consumers receive only what they asked for; Kafka keeps the broker simple with flat topics and pushes filtering to the consumer in exchange for massive throughput and durable replay.
